title: FIX-576: Demo Final Run — End-to-End Walkthrough
description: This tour covers the Demo Final Run (FIX-576), which consolidates and validates fixes from the preceding chain of tickets (FIX-553 through FIX-559). The changes remove the `verification_broken` outcome, add an orchestrator consistency guard, restrict `platform_deferred` to NetSuite UI scenarios, add the `demo` step to RESEARCH and SANDBOX_DEPLOY exclusion sets, and update the client UI with proper demo viewer placement and an ArtifactViewer error boundary. This walkthrough traces the data flow from orchestrator-level outcome logic through server-side step exclusions down to the client rendering layer.

steps.description: This ticket (FIX-576) is the capstone of a multi-ticket fix chain. Its purpose is to review and validate that all prior fixes (FIX-553, FIX-554, FIX-555, FIX-557, FIX-559) are complete, coherent, and that demo workflows function correctly in both BUILD and FIX modes. The ticket references five predecessor tickets materialized under `.helix-refs/`, which supply the actual code artifacts reviewed and finalized in this run. Start here to understand the scope before diving into individual file changes.
steps.title: Overview: Demo Final Run Ticket

steps.description: The five referenced tickets form a logical dependency chain: FIX-553 removes `verification_broken` and adds the orchestrator consistency guard; FIX-554 restricts `platform_deferred` to NetSuite UI scenarios only; FIX-555 adds the `demo` step to RESEARCH and SANDBOX_DEPLOY exclusion sets so demo steps are never incorrectly skipped or included in those modes; FIX-557 updates the client UI (demo viewer placement, ArtifactViewer error boundary, `verification_broken` removal, `platform_deferred` display); FIX-559 addresses any remaining gaps. Understanding this chain is essential — each fix feeds into the next, and FIX-576 confirms they all compose correctly.
steps.title: Referenced Ticket Chain

steps.description: FIX-553 is the root change in the chain. It removes the `verification_broken` outcome (which was a sentinel value that leaked into downstream consumers and caused UI rendering errors) and replaces it with an orchestrator-level consistency guard. This guard ensures that when an agent produces an unexpected or partial result, the orchestrator normalizes the outcome before it is stored or emitted to clients — preventing undefined state from propagating through the pipeline. All subsequent fixes in this chain depend on `verification_broken` being absent.
steps.title: FIX-553: Orchestrator Consistency Guard

steps.description: FIX-554 narrows the conditions under which `platform_deferred` is emitted as an outcome. Previously it could appear in any scenario where the agent could not complete a step, causing confusion in non-NetSuite contexts. After this fix, `platform_deferred` is only valid when the active integration is a NetSuite UI scenario. This change affects the orchestrator's outcome-selection logic and ensures that the client UI's `platform_deferred` display path (added in FIX-557) is only triggered in the correct context.
steps.title: FIX-554: platform_deferred Restricted to NetSuite UI

steps.description: FIX-555 adds the `demo` step identifier to the RESEARCH and SANDBOX_DEPLOY exclusion sets. These sets govern which steps are skipped or suppressed during those execution modes. Without this fix, demo steps could incorrectly execute (or fail to execute) during RESEARCH or SANDBOX_DEPLOY runs, producing misleading output. By explicitly excluding `demo` from these sets, the step lifecycle is correctly scoped: demo steps only run in BUILD and FIX modes where they are meaningful and safe to execute.
steps.title: FIX-555: demo Step Added to Exclusion Sets

steps.description: FIX-557 is the client-side complement to the orchestrator fixes. It makes four targeted changes: (1) moves the demo viewer to its correct placement in the step result layout; (2) wraps ArtifactViewer in an error boundary so a single malformed artifact does not crash the entire results panel; (3) removes all references to `verification_broken` from the UI rendering switch/case and display logic, since that outcome no longer exists after FIX-553; (4) adds a dedicated display path for `platform_deferred` so NetSuite UI deferral is communicated clearly to the user. These UI changes only make sense after the orchestrator normalization in FIX-553 and FIX-554 are in place.
steps.title: FIX-557: Client UI Updates

steps.description: FIX-559 addresses any residual issues discovered after the first four fixes were staged. Its artifacts are also materialized under `.helix-refs/FIX-559/`. At this stop, confirm that FIX-559's changes do not reintroduce `verification_broken`, do not widen `platform_deferred` beyond NetSuite UI, and do not remove `demo` from the exclusion sets. FIX-576 (this run) validates that all five fixes compose without regression.
steps.title: FIX-559: Remaining Gap Resolution

steps.description: After all five referenced fixes are applied and validated by this FIX-576 run, the major code paths are clean: (1) The orchestrator never emits `verification_broken` — all outcomes are normalized at the guard before storage or emission. (2) `platform_deferred` is scoped exclusively to NetSuite UI scenarios, preventing false deferral signals elsewhere. (3) Demo steps are correctly excluded from RESEARCH and SANDBOX_DEPLOY execution modes, running only in BUILD and FIX contexts. (4) The client UI renders all valid outcomes without crashing, with the demo viewer in the correct position and an error boundary protecting the ArtifactViewer. The demo workflows verified in this run confirm end-to-end correctness across both BUILD and FIX modes.
steps.title: Summary: Major Code Paths Remain Clean
